atoms.b:
Certain ideas were central to colonial rule:

Scientific Racism divided humanity into races and claimed that white people were biologically ((superior)) to others. This classification built on “Social Darwinism” and wrongly applied biological ((evolution)) to human societies. Based on this, European scientists argued that stronger races were destined to dominate weaker ones. However, these scientists made ((biased)) interpretations about other “race's” behaviour. What was seen as a fact has been ((disproven)) by modern biology; there is no distinction between humans.

atoms.b: Racism coexisted with the idea of cultural development, which assumed that humanity ((develops)) in a progressive line from “primitive” to more “advanced” ((cultures)). This concept was inherently Eurocentric and placed ((Western_European)) cultures at the top of humanity's development, while other cultures were seen as underdeveloped. Under the guise of ((elevating)) underdeveloped cultures, it was seen as the “White Man's Burden” to ((civilise)) them.

sound/en/f2Poly/Racism coexisted with the idea of cultural development, which assumed that humanity develops in a progressive line from “primitive” to more “advanced” cultures. This concept was inherently Eurocentric and placed Western European cultures at the top of humanity's development, while other cultures were seen as underdeveloped. Under the guise of elevating underdeveloped cultures, it was seen as the “White Man's Burden” to civilise them.
